system: mixed system consisting of English common law, French civil law, and Islamic sharia law

constitution.history: approved and promulgated 11 November 1962; suspended 1976 to 1981 (4 articles); 1986 to 1991; May to July 1999
constitution.amend: proposed by the amir or supported by at least one third of the National Assembly; passage requires two-thirds consent of the Assembly membership and promulgation by the amir; constitutional articles on the initiation, approval, and promulgation of general legislation cannot be amended
constitution.note: in May 2024, Amir Sheikh MISHAL al-Ahmad al-Sabah dissolved the National Assembly and suspended several articles of the constitution for up to four years

courts.highest: Constitutional Court (consists of 5 judges); Supreme Court or Court of Cassation (organized into several circuits, each with 5 judges)
courts.judges: all Kuwaiti judges appointed by the Amir on recommendation of the Supreme Judicial Council, a consultative body comprised of Kuwaiti judges and Ministry of Justice officials
courts.lower: High Court of Appeal; Court of First Instance; Summary Court

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of Kuwait

suffrage: 21 years of age and at least 20-year citizenship
world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICCt
